ogTitle: Thailand Visa Guide for Tourists 2026 — Visa Exemption, Days Allowed, TDAC
ogDesc: A plain-English guide to entering Thailand as a tourist: who gets visa-exemption, how many days you can stay, visa on arrival vs e-Visa, and the new TDAC digital arrival card you fill in before you fly.
intro: Most visitors do not need a visa in advance for a short holiday in Thailand — but the rules change often and depend on your nationality. This guide breaks it down simply, including the digital TDAC arrival card many travelers still miss.

blocks.html: Short answer: Since 15 September 2026, travelers from 60 countries and territories (including the US, UK, EU, Australia, Japan, India and most of ASEAN) enter Thailand visa-free for 30 days, for tourism. Others may use Visa on Arrival or need an e-Visa in advance. Everyone, by air, land or sea, completes the digital arrival card (TDAC) online before arriving.
How you enter depends mainly on your passport. Broadly there are three groups.

blocks.title: Rules change often — check the official source
blocks.html: The number of days and the list of visa-exempt nationalities can change yearly. Before you travel, confirm with a Thai embassy or the Thai government e-Visa website. Do not rely on old blog posts alone.

blocks.text: What is the digital arrival card (TDAC)?

blocks.html: Thailand has moved from the paper TM6 to the Thailand Digital Arrival Card (TDAC) — a free online form every foreign visitor completes before arriving, whether by air, land or sea. Fill it in within the 3 days before you arrive and keep the confirmation to show at the border; it speeds up immigration.

items: It is free — beware fake sites that charge a fee; use only the official Immigration Bureau website
Have your passport number, flight number and first-night address ready
It applies at land borders and seaports too, not only airports

blocks.html: If you want to stay longer, visa-exempt visitors can extend once, by up to 30 days, at an immigration office (฿1,900; the officer decides). Anyone planning a long stay, work or study should get the correct visa type from the start. Never overstay — there is a daily fine and it can affect future entries.

faq.q: Do I need a visa to visit Thailand?
faq.a: Usually not. If your nationality is on the visa-exemption list (which includes many Western and ASEAN countries), you can enter for a short holiday with just your passport. Some nationalities need Visa on Arrival or an e-Visa in advance, so always check for your specific passport before traveling.

faq.q: How many days can I stay visa-free?
faq.a: Since 15 September 2026, most visa-exempt nationalities get 30 days per entry (90 days for South Korea, Brazil, Argentina, Chile and Peru by agreement), and can extend once by up to 30 days at immigration for ฿1,900. The entry-rules box on this page shows the date we last checked.
No. The digital TDAC arrival card is free on the official website. If a site asks you to pay, treat it as a scam.
There is a per-day fine when you leave, and a long overstay can lead to future entry bans. Plan your exit date clearly or extend before your permitted stay ends.

quickAnswerHtml: Since 15 September 2026, travelers from 60 countries and territories (including the US, UK, EU, Australia, Japan, India and most of ASEAN) can enter Thailand visa-free for 30 days for tourism, and can extend once by up to 30 days at an immigration office (฿1,900). South Korea, Brazil, Argentina, Chile and Peru get 90 days by agreement; China and Russia get 30. Other nationalities need Visa on Arrival or an e-Visa in advance. Every foreign visitor completes the free digital arrival card (TDAC) online within the 3 days before arrival.
